explanation: Backtrack through the phone digits using the fixed uppercase keypad mapping. Write one letter into a shared current string per digit and copy each complete mnemonic; zero and one map to themselves.
timeComplexity: O(n · M), where M is the number of mnemonics (at most 4^n). Every completed mnemonic of length n must be copied; there are M product-of-mapping-sizes leaves.
spaceComplexity: O(n) working space, plus O(n · M) output. The mutable word and recursion use O(n); output stores n characters for each of M words.

correctness: At recursion depth i, the prefix contains one allowed letter for each of the first i digits. Trying every mapped letter at the next position preserves validity and covers all continuations. At the final depth, every valid combination has been generated exactly once.
walkthrough: For phone number "30", digit 3 offers D, E and F, and digit 0 offers only 0. The three completed branches are D0, E0 and F0, so return ["D0","E0","F0"].
edgeCases: Digits 0 and 1 remain their own characters.
Digits 7 and 9 each offer four letters.
An empty digit string produces one empty mnemonic.
